persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Grace Miller, 65, the volunteer treasurer of Hope Valley Church in Austin, Texas. Every gift needs a thank-you letter that works as a tax receipt. Today you must get the church's details into the app and write the letters for three gifts.

challenge.intro: Now you are Grace, the treasurer of Hope Valley Church. The app is empty. Nobody will tell you which button to press. Use what you learned. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Use the NORMAL app link (not the 🧪 test copy). Open Receipt Maker. If the welcome tour shows, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own'. Then scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap '🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data' → OK → OK. (If it says 'There is nothing saved in this app yet', tap OK: it is already empty.) All the boxes are now empty and there is one empty gift row.

tasks.text: Put in your church: Hope Valley Church, tax number (EIN) 74-1234567.
tasks.hint: Section 1, Your organization: the first two boxes.

tasks.text: The church is in Austin, Texas, and you, Grace Miller the Treasurer, sign the letters. Put that in.
tasks.hint: Section 1 also has an Address box and a Signer box. The signer needs a name AND a job title.

tasks.text: Mary Johnson gave $500 on 15 March 2026. Peter Brown gave $1,200 on 20 June 2026. Add both gifts.
tasks.hint: Section 2, The gifts: one row per gift, with name, amount and date. Use Add another donor for a second row. Check the amounts and the dates carefully.

tasks.text: David Wilson gave the church a used laptop (no money) on 2 May 2026. Add this gift the right way.
tasks.hint: A gift of a thing, not money, is an in-kind gift. Remember how the video said to write it in the amount box.

tasks.text: Your list must have exactly these three gifts and nothing else. Remove any other rows.
tasks.hint: Each row has a small × at its end to remove it.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: writes thank-you / tax receipt letters for people who gave to a church or charity
you type the organization once and one row per gift (name, amount, date)
makes all the letters at once with the right tax words, ready to print

lines: This is Receipt Maker. In the next few minutes you will see what it is for, who it is for, and exactly how to use it.
Here is the everyday problem. A donor who gives two hundred fifty dollars or more to a church or charity needs a written receipt to claim that gift on their taxes.
That receipt needs certain words the IRS asks for. Leave them out, and the donor's deduction can be at risk.
So every January, a treasurer or a secretary sits down and writes those letters, one at a time. For a small church, that can take a whole weekend.
Receipt Maker is for that person: the volunteer treasurer, the church secretary, or the one-person office of a small nonprofit.
The big idea is simple. You type your organization's details once, list the gifts, and tap one button. It writes a proper letter for every gift, ready to print.
Everything is on one page, from top to bottom. There are no tabs to learn. Section one is called Your organization.
Type the organization name, the EIN, which is your federal tax number, the address, and the signer's name and title, like Treasurer. You do this once.
Section two is called The gifts. Each gift gets one row with three boxes: donor name, amount, and date received.
In the amount box, just type the number. You do not need a dollar sign. The date box opens a calendar.

If someone gave a thing instead of money, like a desk or a computer, type in-kind, a colon, and what it was. For example: in-kind: used office desk. The letter describes the gift without putting a value on it.
To add a row, tap Add another donor. To remove one, tap the small cross at the end of that row.
Have the gifts in a spreadsheet already? Tap Paste a list instead. Paste one gift per line: name, amount, date. Then tap Put these into the boxes.
Under the gifts are two tick boxes. No goods or services starts ticked. Untick it if donors received something, like a dinner, and each letter gets a blank for what they received and its value.
Tick We are a church if you are one. The letter then uses the IRS wording for churches, which mentions intangible religious benefits.
Then tap the big button, Make the letters. You get one letter for each gift, all at once.
If a row is missing a name or an amount, it is not quietly dropped. A note above the letters names every row it skipped, and why.
Each letter has today's date, a warm thank you, the gift and its date, the right tax wording, and the signer's name.
Tap any letter to change its words, perhaps to add a personal line.
Then tap Print them all. Each letter prints on its own page, without the boxes and buttons. Sign them, and they are ready to mail.
Your first two minutes: fill in Your organization, add one real gift, and tap Make the letters. Read that letter before you do the whole list.
Your organization and gift rows stay saved on this device. The letters are made fresh each time, with one tap. Start fresh, at the very bottom, clears it all, and asks twice first.
No account is needed, and donor names stay on your own device. It works without a connection, too.
One honest note, printed right in the app: this is not tax advice. When in doubt, ask your accountant.
Receipt Maker comes with the Small charity membership, or with the Church membership. Any profit helps orphans and students in Kenya.
And the round question mark button has the tour and help, any time.

daily.task: Make one new receipt in Receipt Maker for a made-up gift (a made-up name and amount). Don’t send or share it.

explore.name: 🏢 Section 1 · Your organization
explore.find: Open Receipt Maker. It is the top section.
explore.try: Fill name, EIN, address and signer. In EIN try letters, and only 5 numbers.

explore.name: 🎁 Section 2 · The gifts
explore.try: Fill three rows: a couple, a big amount like 1,200, and “in-kind”. Pick dates. Remove a row with ×. Tap ✚ Add another donor.

explore.name: 📋 Paste a list
explore.try: Paste three lines like “Mary Smith, 250, 2026-03-14”. Put these into the boxes. Then try one bad line.

explore.name: ☑️ The two tick boxes
explore.try: Untick “No goods or services” and tick “We are a church”. See the letters change.

explore.name: ✉️ Make the letters
explore.try: Make them with one row missing its amount — does it say which row it skipped and why?

explore.name: ✏️ Change a letter · 🖨 Print
explore.try: Change its words. Tap 🖨 Print them all (cancel the printer).

explore.name: ❓ The round ? button
explore.find: Tap the round ? in the bottom corner.
explore.try: Open every line in it: Aa (size), ✨ Ask an AI, 🌉 More from Daraja, 🎬 Take the tour again. Close it. Leave “Start fresh” for the very end.
